theory.intro: A figure lets you travel from one point to another along vectors you already know. Add the steps tip to tail, and reverse a vector whenever you travel against its arrow.
facts: **Triangle law**: $\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}$, so a journey through $B$ collapses to the direct step.
**Negative vector law**: $\overrightarrow{AB}=-\overrightarrow{BA}$, so travelling backwards along an arrow changes its sign.
**Parallelogram law of subtraction**: $\overrightarrow{AB}-\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{DB}$, the journey from $D$ back to $A$ and on to $B$.
If $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$ then $\overrightarrow{AM}=\frac{1}{2}\overrightarrow{AB}$.
A result is proved by writing both sides in terms of the same given vectors and showing they agree.
steps: Choose a route through the figure from the start point to the end point
Write each step in terms of the given vectors

development.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{OM}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{ON}=\underset{\sim}{b}$
$\overrightarrow{MN}$
$=\overrightarrow{ON}-\overrightarrow{OM}$
$=\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}$
$\overrightarrow{AB}$
$=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}$
$=2\underset{\sim}{b}-2\underset{\sim}{a}$
$=2\left(\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}\right)$
So $\overrightarrow{AB}=2\overrightarrow{MN}$, which means $MN$ is parallel to $AB$ and half its length.

mastery.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{MA}=\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{a}$
$\overrightarrow{AB}=\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}$
$\overrightarrow{AN}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}\right)$
$\overrightarrow{MN}$
$=\overrightarrow{MA}+\overrightarrow{AN}$
$=\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{a}+\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{b}-\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{a}$
$=\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{b}$
So $\overrightarrow{MN}=\frac{1}{2}\overrightarrow{OB}$, a scalar multiple of $\overrightarrow{OB}$, which means $MN$ is parallel to $OB$.
